rationale.complete: Round 1 done on 13 periods (24 testable units, 12 descriptive): card and dated predictions, synthetic checks on 4 real unit skeletons (5 worlds, floors and price recovery; A1 fixed before data), max-ent hierarchy with three floors and agent-block bootstraps, replication on every unit, 3 natives (G35 room assignment, G44 planned vs free, G40 NE42 merge), 142 estimate rows, frozen guarded confirm script (dry-run only).
rationale.faithfulness: HH285's core claim holds in a refined form: with episodes as the unit and the run-persistence floor, the residual after margins + ownership (+ rooms) is <= 0.13 of I(agent; repo) in 23/24 units (inside the 95% band in 12/24). Ownership price separates goal types (p = 0.0007) and responds to the NE42 merge as predicted. Against: P1, P6, P7, P8 and the G44 native failed; the floor and episode unit were chosen after the synthetic (A1); near-saturation of the max-ent model makes small residuals partly by construction; #51 keeps a significant 0.1-0.3 bit residual. C = 1, D = 1, E = 1, F = 1, G = 2.
rationale.usefulness: Gives a monitor two summary numbers per week (ownership price, episode concentration) and a measured lever: own-artifact goals raise lambda_own from ~2 to ~8 nats, a merge onto one named target lowers it by >= 7 nats. Shows there is no hidden plan or extra specialization to recover from allocation data. The herding index needs an activity-free version before it is actionable.
